newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore court says politician can appeal on libel.
newsitem.headline: Singapore court says politician can appeal on libel.

text.p: The Singapore High Court said on Friday opposition politician Tang Liang Hong could appeal in the cases which led to the award of Singapore $8.08 million (US$5.65 million) in libel damages against him.

The court dismissed a move by lawyers for Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and senior colleagues to stop Tang appealing against decisions in the cases which culminated in them winning record damages on Thursday.
Justice Goh Joon Seng said Tang had two weeks to file an appeal to a three-judge bench.

Tang's lawyer, Worker's Party leader Joshua Jeyaretnam, told the court that refusing leave to appeal would only give Tang more ammunition in his fight with Goh and other leaders of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP).
"To refuse him will only give him further material to say that he can't get justice," Jeyaretnam said.
Tang was a Worker's Party candidate in January 2 general elections in which the PAP won all but two of the 83 seats at stake.
He became the major issue in the campaign when Goh called him "an anti-English educated, anti-Christian chauvinist" who endangered Singapore's racial harmony.
Tang, who fled Singapore after the losing his election fight saying he had received death threats, accused Goh and other PAP members who backed their leader on the issue of lying.
They hit him with 13 libel suits over various remarks, saying their integrity, crucial to leadership of thriving Singapore, had been attacked.
Tang lost all the cases in March when he failed to return to Singapore to defend himself.
Goh and his colleagues demanded S$12.9 million in aggravated damages, accusing Tang of continuing to malign them in media interviews after the cases were filed.
On Thursday, the court agreed with the PAP leaders that they deserved aggravated damages.
Tang said he would appeal against the award.
"Surely I an not satisfied with this because to me they are not entitled to one cent," Tang told Reuters by telephone from Hong Kong.
He had already filed an appeal against the March verdict that he had committed libel and against his failure to remove a judge from the case.
Tang had alleged that Justice Lai Kew Chai was close to former prime minister Lee Kuan Yew, one of the PAP leaders suing him.
A furious Lai accused Tang of scurrilous fabrication, denied any relationship with Lee and refused to step down.
Tang has also been charged with 33 counts of tax evasion and an arrest warrant has been issued for him.
Tang faces a fine three times the amount of tax he is accused of evading -- S$211,000 -- plus a fince of $$10,000 per charge. He could also be jailed for three years on each charge.
